chunk_findings.detail: When `--lane` is used, `_next` computes `tags = _tags(a)` but then calls `_api().next_lane(...)` without passing `tags`, while the non-lane path passes `tags=tags` to `next_item`. Thus `ddflow next --lane L --tag wave:3` (or `--wave 3`) accepts the tag filter but the lane answer is produced from the unfiltered lane candidate set, so an item lacking `wave:3` can still be offered; this violates the stated falsifier that no item without the requested tag may appear in ready/blocked.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next

chunk_findings.detail: The queue fixture creates no dependency relationships, so the normal `next` output for this fixture has an empty `blocked` list. The assertion `all(b["item"] in {"M.A", "M.B"} for b in d["blocked"])` is therefore vacuously true and does not demonstrate that blocked items are filtered by `--tag`; if the implementation failed to filter blocked items in a queue that does have blocked tasks, this test would still pass. This contradicts the stated test goal that ready and blocked items are limited to the tag.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_next_tag_filter.py:test_tag_limits_ready_and_blocked

chunk_findings.detail: `--tag` / `--wave` are parsed into `tags` and passed only on the no-lane path. `ddflow next --lane L --tag x` (or `--wave 0`) still calls `next_lane` without those tags, so an item that does not carry the tag is offered whenever it is next on that lane. The flags are accepted and then dropped, which is a silent wrong answer rather than a refusal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next

chunk_findings.detail: The lane branch computes `tags = _tags(a)` but then calls `_api().next_lane(...)` without passing `tags`, so `--tag`/`--wave` are silently ignored whenever `--lane` is used. For example, `ddflow next --lane <lane> --tag wave:3` (or `--wave 3`) can return ready/blocked items from that lane that lack `wave:3`, and an unknown tag in lane mode is not refused, contrary to the declared `next` parameters and the added workflow help.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next

chunk_findings.detail: `test_tag_limits_ready_and_blocked` does not actually exercise blocked filtering. The `_queue` fixture creates tasks with no dependencies or other blocking conditions, so `d["blocked"]` is empty for the `--tag x` call; the assertion `all(b["item"] in {"M.A", "M.B"} for b in d["blocked"])` is therefore vacuously true. If the implementation failed to filter blocked items—for example, if an untagged task that is blocked by a dependency were returned in `blocked`—this test would still pass, despite the intent requiring that both ready and blocked be limited to the tag.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_next_tag_filter.py:74-78

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_queue` fixture violates the recorded project rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave]: every task must name a phase, state dependencies in `needs`, and carry a `wave:N` tag, with `no-deps` for prerequisite-free work. Here `M.A`, `M.B`, and `N.C` have wave tags but no `no-deps` despite having no `--needs`, and `N.D` is created with no tags at all, so it has neither a wave tag nor `no-deps`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_next_tag_filter.py:13-64

chunk_findings.detail: `candidates = with_tags(candidates, tags)` filters the candidate items *before* the planning and cap computation loop (`plan()` body), violating the requirement: "Filter applied to the candidates BEFORE the cap cut, so the cap is computed over the whole queue as now." Because `candidates` is restricted to only those matching `tags` prior to calculating parallelism limits, slot counts, and ready/blocked partitions, the cap is computed exclusively over the filtered slice rather than the whole queue.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule/_plan.py:289

chunk_findings.detail: `--tag` / `--wave` are declared on the same `next` command as `--lane`, and `_tags` is computed for every call, but the `--lane` branch still calls `next_lane` without `tags`. Given a lane that offers both `M.A` (tag `x`) and `N.D` (no `x`), `ddflow next --lane that-lane --tag x` returns `N.D` in ready or blocked. That is the stated falsifier: an item lacking the tag appears, and the flag is silently ignored rather than exiting 1 or intersecting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next
